name: Concept F: Chirped pellet slipstream
description: Exotic and speculative (TRL 2). Matches analysis/ideas_calc.py: 10,000 pellets of 0.375 g (3.75 kg total) are ionised and magnetically reflected by a 2 kg probe at a fixed 100 km/s relative speed and 80% momentum-transfer efficiency. This supplies 300 km/s delta-v with about 131 GJ ideal pellet launch energy. The reference starts at solar escape speed at 5 AU (18.837 km/s) and debits a conservative 30-day gravity-loss bound of 0.615 km/s. The initial ellipse encodes that already-debited speed (18.223 km/s) at its 5 AU perihelion, so a prograde equivalent impulse gives solar v∞ 317.665 km/s. This represents a scalar speed budget, not the actual 30-day powered trajectory. Probe mass stays constant because reflected pellets are expelled. The preview shows only the post-impulse coast; launch, delivery to 5 AU, aiming, ionisation, heating and powered-flight steering are not simulated. Showstopper: pellet-stream aiming and ionisation over AU scales; one un-ionised pellet destroys the probe.

events.notes: Launch successive pellets faster as the probe accelerates, keeping relative speed at 100 km/s. Ideal reflection gives Δv = 2 × 0.8 × 100 × 3.75 / 2 = 300 km/s. The initial state already debits the reference 30-day gravity allowance; do not subtract it again. About 131 GJ is the ideal launch kinetic energy summed over probe speeds 0–300 km/s in the launcher frame, excluding initial heliocentric motion, launch and ionisation losses. Equivalent impulse at 5 AU; no finite-thrust propagation.
